topics.topic: Error classification and lookup order for missing add_captured_trial_case references
questions: If the implementation, named contract version, source NodeExecution, or referenced SpooledFile is missing, does `functions.add_captured_trial_case` return `unknown_reference` under the global convention or `refused` under its operation-specific Errors section, and in what lookup order?

If the implementation, contract version, source NodeExecution, StoredValue or SpooledFile named to this operation is missing, is the result `unknown_reference`, `refused`, or `internal_error` because the caller was trusted?

What error is returned when the implementation, contract version, source execution or referenced SpooledFile does not exist: `unknown_reference` under the global convention, or `refused` under this operation's Errors section?

quotes: add_captured_trial_case: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST first read the Implementation of executed_implementation_id from its own records, UnknownReferenceError propagating; then raises RefusedError naming the first failing check: that implementation's contract_version_id differs from named_contract_version_id; then each input port in port name order does not fit by fit_port_value, values read from their StoredValues and checked against the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant, each spooled file of a SpooledFilesRef taken by its SpooledFile facts, its media type equal to the port's and its size_bytes within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRIAL_FIX_BYTES_MAX constant; every check comes before any byte is copied, so a refusal copies and writes nothing.

read_records: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST first raise StoreInternalError, before any record is looked up, when the query's arguments are malformed for its kind (a record_type that has no such identity form, an empty identity list or a field of another kind); then raise UnknownReferenceError naming the first missing record, in the order given for identity queries and in the order the relation's fields name them for a relation (an ElementKey names its run); a corpus digest is a value and is never missing, RunsByStatus and AttemptsByStatus name no record, and ActivationBeforeRun finding no activation raises StoreInternalError.

capture_failed_execution: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST copy nothing itself: after its own checks it calls add_captured_trial_case with the implementation_id of the record's ExecutedImplementation, the named contract version, the record's inputs as they are — a StoredValuesRef as it is and spooled files as their SpooledFilesRef —, the AttemptKey and the actor, and returns its TrialCase; a refusal of add_captured_trial_case propagates as it is and has copied nothing.
judgement.why: The later notes specify that the implementation lookup and missing referenced records propagate UnknownReferenceError, a mismatching named contract version is RefusedError, inputs are checked in port-name order, and the source execution is validated by the calling capture operation.

topics.topic: Raw bytes, digest rule, and module used to compute file content digests and facts
questions: What exact bytes are hashed for a file fixture or SpooledFile, since arbitrary file bytes have no RFC 8785 canonical JSON representation, and which module computes that digest before file facts are checked?
Are `content_digest` and file-fixture digests SHA-256 of the raw file bytes, or of some JSON representation of those bytes?
Which module computes file facts from bytes, by what operation, and under which digest rule?
What exact bytes are hashed for a file's `value_digest` or `content_digest`?

quotes: content_identity: [BEHAVIOR] For the json_text variant MUST return the hexadecimal SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of json_text, and for the bytes variant the hexadecimal SHA-256 of content exactly as given, without any canonicalization; this is the digest of a file and of a value's bytes.

add_trial_case: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] Each input value becomes a StoredValue with the stored schema of its port (M21: the port's value_schema, or for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items) and the class its contract input port declares, each expected output a StoredValue with its port's stored schema and the highest class of the case's inputs from highest_disclosure_class; value_digest is content_identity of the bytes, value_id content_identity of the StoredValueContent, and the bytes are stored with put_value_bytes; a port refers to its values by a StoredValuesRef, one value_id per file in list order for a many file port.

spool_file: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns FileFacts with the hexadecimal SHA-256 content_digest, size_bytes and the given media_type; it writes no SpooledFile record, which the caller's later record_change writes.
judgement.why: The later notes define file digests as SHA-256 of the exact raw bytes: canonical_values.content_identity computes fixture/value-byte digests through its bytes variant, while store.spool_file computes and returns spooled-file facts.

precedent.topic: Allowed api_base_url forms and derivation of joined URLs, authority, Host, and connection target
quotes:
the installation selects no instance for the service or that
   instance has no `api_base_url` — one that is not an absolute `http` or
   `https` URL with a host counts as none — or names one required header
   twice, or names one the kernel sets itself (`host`, `accept-encoding`,
   `content-type`, `content-length`, A10 rule 7) other than `host`, which an
   instance may set instead of the kernel (A10 rule 7), names compared without
   regard to case — at send time both are A09 rule 6's `required_header_repeated`
   —, or has a required header whose name is not an HTTP field-name token, or whose value is empty, has leading or trailing whitespace, or holds a control character — at send time `required_header_invalid`;

The
   URL is the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared
   path, which must start with one `/` and contain no `//`, no `.` or `..`
   segment, no `?` or `#`, and no scheme or host; a `{` or `}` appears only in a
   placeholder, which is one whole segment `{name}` whose name is not empty and
   contains no `{`, `}` or `/`, and no name is a placeholder twice; a path that
   does not is not invocable (A08 rule 3). Placeholder values are percent-encoded so that they
   stay one segment. Nothing else is normalized.

Plain `http` is allowed only for an instance of
   class `local_dev` or `disposable_rig`, as the manifest instance's `class`
   states — an absent or unknown class counts as `production` — or one whose
   `api_base_url` host is a loopback address; any other plain `http` target is refused before sending.
   The host judged here, the one connected to, and for `https` the server name
   sent and verified, are always those of `api_base_url`; a required `Host`
   header (A10 rule 7) changes only the header sent.

`host` — the authority of `api_base_url` exactly as the manifest writes it,
   not normalized (A09 rule 1), unless the instance's required headers name
   `host`, in which case that required header is sent instead, its value
   verbatim, and is the only `host` —, `accept-encoding: identity` (A09 rule 3),
precedent.why: The texts constrain an absolute HTTP(S) URL and simple concatenation but do not close the accepted URL grammar, slash handling, component interaction, or loopback classification.

precedent.topic: Input representation and duplicate-key detection for canonical JSON
quotes: canonical_bytes: [BEHAVIOR] MUST parse json_text as one JSON value and emit its RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical form encoded as UTF-8: object members sorted by the UTF-16 code units of their names, numbers written in the ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (an integral double without a fraction or exponent, so a number written 1.0 becomes 1), strings escaped exactly as JCS prescribes, and no whitespace; it applies no Unicode normalization, so two texts that differ only in normalization give different bytes.

canonical_bytes: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order, when json_text is not one well-formed JSON value, when an object repeats a member name at any depth, when it holds a non-finite number (NaN, Infinity or -Infinity tokens, which the default Python parser would accept and therefore MUST be rejected explicitly), when a number written without a fraction or exponent lies outside plus or minus (2 to the power 53 minus 1), which an IEEE double cannot hold exactly, or when a string holds a lone surrogate.
precedent.why: State 6 specifies that canonical_bytes receives and parses JSON text, preserving duplicate-member information until validation.

precedent.topic: Startup validation scope and ordering for installed service records and capabilities
quotes: read_service_record: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Raises RefusedError naming the first failing check of the record itself, in this order: the record is absent at that revision, is not valid JSON, lacks service or capabilities, its service field differs from service_id, two capabilities share a name.

check_installed_instances: [VALIDATION_ERROR] Takes the services the installation holds a credential for, in service_id order by Unicode code point, and for each raises RefusedError naming that service at the first failure: first the credential header name equals a name in the imported KERNEL_SET_HEADER_NAMES constant compared without regard to case, host included, checked without reading the manifest; then, only when the installation selects an instance for the service, its record read by read_service_record fails any check, or the selected instance named in the record has a required header whose name equals the credential header name compared without regard to case.

check_installed_instances: [BEHAVIOR] A service with no selected instance, or whose record lists no instance of the selected name, fails nothing here; the check reads only the given installation and the manifest, never the store, and returns None when every service passes.
precedent.why: The later notes limit startup validation to credential-bearing services, ordered by service_id, and to top-level service-record checks plus the selected instance's credential-header collision.
